subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit Slack user-identity DM mode that receives and replies as a regular Slack user via xoxp tokens?
rationale: This changes Slack identity, authorization, and audit semantics; source shows the current contract is bot-first with user tokens used mainly for reads, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary alone.

options.title: Design explicit user mode
options.body: Keep this issue open for a plugin-owned opt-in mode with authorization mapping, xoxp reply routing, security docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Keep bot identity only
options.body: Document bot/app DM behavior as the supported Slack path and decline user-identity control unless a maintainer later sponsors it.

options.title: Request live repro first
options.body: Ask for redacted Socket Mode/user-event proof before deciding whether the feature is worth the security and product cost.

recommendation.title: Design explicit user mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a plugin-owned opt-in mode with authorization mapping, xoxp reply routing, security docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original user-token feature and recent Slack auth work, making him the strongest available routing candidate for the product/security decision.
